sections.h2: Who records deeds in Lawrence County, Pennsylvania?
sections.html:
The Register of Wills and Recorder of Deeds, a combined office serving the county seat of New Castle. Its page on the county website calls the Recorder's main duty recording, protecting, preserving and reproducing legal documents that relate to real estate.

The same office collects county recording fees, the Real Estate Transfer Tax owed to the state, local municipalities and school districts, and the fees that state law sends to the Administrative Office of Pennsylvania Courts. For anyone selling a house in Lawrence County, that means one counter takes the tax and the fee and files the deed.

Ask the office for its current hours and its last time to accept a deed on a given day, since a title company's schedule depends on it.

sections.h2: How far back do Lawrence County land records go, and can I search them online?
sections.html:
Records reach back to the founding of the county in 1849, and all real estate records are open to the public. Staff say older books are searched in the office, while more recent years can be searched online.

The online service runs on CountyFusion and lets you search, view and print documents dating to about 1970. The county also offers a quick land-records search from its cloud search page, and a free property alert service launched in October 2022 that warns an owner when a document is recorded against their property.

  • Use the online index to pull the previous deed and copy the legal description exactly.
  • Check that the name on the old deed matches the name of the person signing the new one.
  • Look for old mortgages that still show as open, and ask the lender for a satisfaction if one was paid off.

sections.h2: Can a Lawrence County deed be recorded electronically?
sections.html:
Yes. The office tells submitters that e-recording is simple, fast and saves money, and it names four vendors on its website: Simplifile, CSC, Indecomm and EPN. Closing agents who already use one of these can send the deed in without a courier.

Paper still works. A deed can be carried in or mailed to the Recorder, but then you need the exact total in the right form, so call the office for a figure before you write a check. The county's Recorder page links notices about about a state-mandated fee increase dated November 28, 2025 and a separate increase in the parcel ID fee.

sections.h2: What does recording a deed cost in Lawrence County?
sections.html:
A fee sheet from the county's Redevelopment Authority, dated September 29, 2026, gives a concrete picture for a deed. It lists deed recording at $87.75 plus $20.00 for each parcel purchased.

Recording charges on the Redevelopment Authority of Lawrence County fee schedule, as of September 29, 2026
ItemAmount
Deed recording$87.75
Added per parcel purchased$20.00
Realty transfer tax2% (1% state, 1% local)
Statement of Value, if tax exempt$2.00

That sheet applies to Authority property sales, so a private sale may differ. Treat the numbers as a guide and get the real total from the Recorder, because the add-ons change with the page count and the number of parcels.

The county's Assessment Office assigns parcel IDs, and it provides a form to request a new one. A deed that covers more than one parcel will therefore cost more to record.

sections.h2: How does transfer tax work on a Lawrence County sale?
sections.html:
Pennsylvania imposes a 1 percent state tax on the value of the transfer, and the Department of Revenue holds both grantor and grantee liable. In the Lawrence County fee sheet the local share is another 1 percent, for a combined 2 percent.

The Recorder remits the state's part to Harrisburg and the rest to the municipality and school district. Certain family transfers, transfers to government, and property that passes by will or intestacy are exempt, but a Statement of Value is still filed to show why.

  • For a sale at $100,000, the combined 2 percent tax would be $2,000, before recording fees.
  • A sale to an outside buyer is an ordinary transfer, so an estate selling a house should plan for the tax in its settlement figures.
  • If title first passes to an heir, the Register of Wills side of the same office can say what paperwork it wants.

sections.h2: What does the Lawrence County Assessment Office handle for a seller?
sections.html:
It values the county's roughly 56,000 parcels, which cover 367 square miles across 27 municipalities. One of them is the city of New Castle, with 8 wards, and the others are nine boroughs and sixteen townships. Ellwood City's second ward lies partly in Beaver County.

The office also runs the Act 72 Homestead and Farmstead Exclusion and the Clean and Green program, and it keeps the county's GIS tax maps. Its forms page lists a sales verification form, a change of address form, and a property owner contact form tied to Act 29 of 2026.

The Assessment Board meets monthly, and the county posts agendas for each 2026 meeting. If you sell a homestead property, ask the office how the sale affects the exclusion and update your mailing address with its change of address form.

sections.h2: What is Lawrence County like for someone who has to sell a house?
sections.html:
Lawrence County was created on March 20, 1849, from parts of Beaver and Mercer counties, when New Castle was outgrowing its home county. It covers 363 square miles in the Greater Pittsburgh region and drains through the Shenango and Mahoning rivers into the Beaver River. South New Castle borough was annexed by Shenango Township on January 1, 2026. I-76, I-79, I-376 and US 422 cross the county.

sections.h2: What should I bring to record a Lawrence County deed?
sections.html:
Pull these together before the closing date.

  • The signed, notarized deed with the full legal description.
  • The parcel ID for each parcel being conveyed.
  • A Statement of Value if tax is excused or the price is not stated.
  • Payment for the recording fee, the parcel ID charge and the transfer tax, in the form the office accepts.
  • A return address for the recorded deed.

If a title company is handling the sale, confirm that they file electronically through one of the four vendors and ask when the recorded copy will arrive.

faqs.q: Does Lawrence County accept electronic recording?
faqs.a: Yes. The Recorder of Deeds lists four e-recording vendors on the county site: Simplifile, CSC, Indecomm and EPN. A closing agent with an account at one of them can submit the deed without a trip to New Castle.

faqs.q: How far back can I search Lawrence County deeds online?
faqs.a: The online system covers documents from about 1970 forward. County records start with the formation of the county in 1849, and the older volumes are searched in the office.

faqs.q: How much is transfer tax on a Lawrence County home sale?
faqs.a: The combined rate in the county's fee sheet is 2 percent, made up of 1 percent state tax and 1 percent local tax. On a $100,000 sale that is $2,000. Exempt transfers, such as some family transfers, file a Statement of Value instead.

faqs.q: Is there a way to be warned if someone records a document on my property?
faqs.a: Yes. The county announced a free property alert service in October 2022. It is meant as fraud protection, and the Recorder's page lists it among its press releases.

faqs.q: What office issues parcel IDs in Lawrence County?
faqs.a: The county Assessment Office. It posts a Request for a New Parcel ID Number form, and it can tell you which parcels a deed must name. Every parcel on a deed adds to the recording cost.
